en: ...Is this about that game in our second year?
Bingo. It was the summer regional final... the qualifier for us to go to nationals at Koshien Stadium.

What's wrong? Why don't you open your mouth and say
something? I know I'm not speaking gibberish here.
No. I know you're not.

Then what, you'd rather forget what you did? Or maybe you
can't even stand the thought of it. Well, allow me to jog
your memory.
The game that everything rode on was locked in a pitchers' duel. Me, the ace of West Kamuro, versus Akamatsu, a monster who could throw at 150 kilometers an hour.
It was the bottom of the ninth, score tied at 0. We had two outs, but also runners on second and third. It was a perfect setup for you to bang out a walk-off home run.
Guess even a beast like Akamatsu must've been nervous, what with a ticket to Koshien on the line. He ended up giving away three balls and no strikes.
On his fourth pitch, he deliberately threw a fastball outside the strike zone.
His reasoning was simple⑬first base was open. So instead of giving the cleanup hitter his big chance, it was safer to walk you instead.
You could have easily walked to first, but no, you just had to swing at that wild pitch. Which became a pop fly that went right into the infielder's glove.
That out caused the game to go into extra innings. But at the top of the tenth, their batters ran me ragged. We got destroyed.
...Then you quit the team the day after, and even left the school. Heard it was 'cause you blew out your shoulder.
My shoulder was wrecked, all right. But that's not why I quit. It was because I was betrayed by the guy I trusted the most.
You mean...
Yeah. You.
Shirakawa...
After my dreams of baseball went spiraling down the drain, I joined a small printing company. The year after, I watched you play at Koshien on TV.
The entire time, I never stopped wondering why you went for that wild pitch instead of taking the walk.
It took a couple years, but I finally got my answer. When you batted for the big leagues your one and only time.
What are you getting at, Shirakawa?

I'm saying you're the kind of scum who puts himself ahead of
the team. That only your own victory matters!
How could you say that!?

Everyone knew Akamatsu was the tournament's top pitcher.
I mean, you couldn't get a single hit off him the entire
game.

But you wanted to prove yourself, didn't you? That you were
good enough to hit one of Akamatsu's pitches... that you
were better than everyone else!

Why else would you swing at an outside pitch on a
three-and-nothing count!? Like a fucking amateur!?
If only you had walked, we'd have been set for a game-winning hit. But there was no guarantee you'd get another chance to bat. So you went ahead and blew it.
That's not true! I read that pitch to the best of my ability. And I went for it because I was sure I could win it for the team.
But, at the time, I simply didn't have what it took to get a hit off Akamatsu. That's all it was, man.
Don't feed me that crap! You can say any damned thing you want in retrospect, but that doesn't change what you did.
You talk like it was some miscalculation, but I know better. The only reason you pulled that stunt back then was to satisfy your own ego. And I'm going to prove it to you.
...How?

By making you relive Akamatsu's pitching from twenty years
back! That's how, Shinada!
That's crazy talk!

You yourself said you didn't have what it took <Italic>at the time</Italic>.
That means you think you could pull it off now. Right?

Hold on. Shirakawa, are you seriously asking me to go up
against Akamatsu from back in our high-school heyday?
I'd, like, need a time machine for that!
No, dumbass. I'll be doing the pitching. I can replicate Akamatsu's style flawlessly.
What about your shoulder?
To hell with that! Point is, if you can hit what I throw, I'll know you had the skills, and chalk it all up a harmless error.
But if you choke, that means you were shit to begin with. It'll be proof that you robbed me of baseball for your own pride. And I will make you pay.
Is this what drove you to search for me all these years? To figure out what was going on in my head?
Okay then. If that's what'll make you happy, I'll gladly get a hit off you.
Sakai-san. Explain yourself. What's going on?
You look well, Shinada. You too, Uno-san.
I know it's not fair... But forgive us, Shinada. Forgive me.
First you apologize, and then you put a weapon in your hands?
Shinada, do you know the most beautiful play a batter can make?
It's a sacrifice fly.
He sacrifices himself for the good of the team. He doesn't get on base, but he contributes more than anyone.
Shinada, I'll never forget what you did! So forgive me!
(Here we are. Just gotta climb down that manhole and use the tunnel to get to <Color:7>Purgatory<Color:Default>.)
Friend of yours?
Not a chance. He's one of the Omi Alliance executives.
That guy's Omi? Didn't exactly look the part.
Naoki Katsuya, age 45. He's a former actor who runs an entertainment company called Osaka Talent. In Osaka, of course.
And behind the scenes, he runs Ousaka Enterprises, an Omi affiliate.
He's known as a likable, courteous businessman with a bright future ahead of him.
...Who would ever guess that he's also in the criminal underworld, one step away from claiming the Omi throne?
His name's Katsuya, huh? I've heard that name before.
Is it possible you've met him?
Nah. I don't forget meetin' anyone. Anyway, what's an Omi man doin' in Kamurocho?
Who knows? He's a public figure; he can pretty much go anywhere, do anything.
Things should stay quiet if he's here on business for Osaka Talent, but if it's for anything involving his other job...
What's the move, then? You want me to go after Morinaga or Katsuya?
I'll keep an eye on Katsuya. You stay on Morinaga's trail, like we planned.
I'll be in touch again tomorrow. Until then.
(Guess I'll start doin' recon on Morinaga. And for that sorta thing, there's one place ya go first.)
(<Color:7>Purgatory<Color:Default>... The way in's through the tunnel under the manhole in Children's Park.)
Why so serious?
Took yer time, didn't ya? Thought ya weren't gonna be that long.
Ooh, my bad. Just having a little trouble at work.
Some internal dissension, you might say.
In the prefectural police?
We're human, just like everybody else. So when a case drags on and on, there are always one or two slackers who want out.
Somehow it's me left with the cleanup. A lotta these kids need to grow up and stop dreaming.
What was your plan if I'd just run off?
Beg the Metro police to do their jobs for once, watch as they close the net around you, smile, and take a nap since you'd be off my hands. I plan everything, my man.
Tch. You must not know how easy it is to hide in this town.
Once ya go to ground, you're as good as gone. Plenty of places where the police can't get ya.
You mean the sewer tunnels under Kamurocho? And that place called Purgatory down there?
Hmph, I know more than you think. You ought to give the police a little more credit.
So whaddya want from me?
You're going to find Morinaga for us.
Yeah. We know that he came back to Tokyo after the incident in Fukuoka.
But we lost track of him after that.
He hasn't been back to Tojo Clan HQ?
No. He shot the acting chairman. He'd be a fool to show his face there now.
But where could he've gone?
That's up to you to figure out. He's in hiding <Italic>somewhere</Italic> in this town.
Where would someone go if he found out he was on the Tojo hit list?
Underground.
Right. Literally! He probably scampered down into the sewers, and now he's hoping to meet up with the rat king who's behind all of this.
If police went down there he'd have plenty of warning time, and he'd slip through our fingers for the umpteenth time.
That's why we need you to find him.
Here's the place.
Okay, no rush. If you have anything else to take care of before going in, I can just wait here for you.
Yeah, wait here for me. I still have a few errands to run.
It's cool. Just don't take too long.
Nah, let's go in and hear what you have to say.
After you, then.
Man... I'd heard the legends about you, but I didn't think they could be true...
I purposely left you enough of your face so you could tell me why you're here.
Not for you to kiss my ass.
Hah, wow. You're just like him. Figures.
Like who?
How do you know Saejima?
You know, I think you might actually have it in you to stop us.
Forgive my rudeness, Kazuma Kiryu-san. My name is Shigeki Baba.
Forget the introductions. Get to the point.
Fine. I'll tell you all about the mess you're caught up in now.
...And what Morinaga has in store.
If you've got the time, that is.
Just spill it.
Could we take it somewhere else?
Somewhere more private, I mean.
Don't even think about making a run for it.
I won't. I owe it to Saejima-san to stop running away from things.
He gave me a pass on that front back in Sapporo. But I don't think I'll get more passes.
You still haven't said how you know him.
Don't worry. I'll get to that, too.
First, let's find a place to talk.
If anyone finds out I blabbed to you... I'm done for.
Fine. I know a place nearby called <Color:7>New Serena<Color:Default>.
We'll have privacy there.
Okay. As long as you're sure about that. Lead the way.
I know you're following me. How about showing your face instead of skulking in the shadows?
So observant... I guess I shouldn't be surprised.
Kazuma Kiryu-san, right?
Who are you? Why were you tailing me?
Someone told me you might show up in Tokyo, and I've been waiting.
I know what happened in Fukuoka. Word is you single-handedly put a stop to Aoyama's entire scheme.
It seems the Dragon of Dojima is breathing fire again.
You must be one of Morinaga's lackeys.
More like a collaborator, I think.
It's not like he's paying me long-term.
So you're not with the Tojo?
No. We just came together because we have the same goals.
There's something I want to ask you, Kiryu-san.
Should I assume that your coming to Tokyo means you're prepared to get involved with this matter? Because it goes deeper than you think.
Dramatics won't work on me.
I'll take that as a yes. That's good.
It's "good"?
Yeah, because if Majima's death hadn't been enough to draw you out of Fukuoka...
We would've had to change our plans.
Were you the ones who killed Majima!?
Touchy. What would you do if I said yes?
I'd drop you right here, and make you sputter through blood the name of whoever's puppeting you.
I was hoping... that you'd try to understand. But since you'd rather get violent.
Only children believe in dragons.
I got that reservation!
The one in Kamurocho Hills? Seriously? I thought it was impossible unless you know someone!
Hehe. I'd move mountains for you, Tomiko-chan.
I can't wait! They're supposed to have the juiciest steak ever! I'm gonna order a huge slab of nice, bloody meat!
Uh... awesome.
(Sounds like Kamurocho Hills is open now.)
Hey, is Kazuki or Yuya around? Tell them Kiryu's asking. They'll understand.
I'm sorry, but neither the owner nor the manager are in yet.
Hm... Look, I've been away from Kamurocho for a while. How are things lately?
You know, it's weird. I haven't seen any yakuza around here the past few days.
I mean, my manager usually chases them away, but he definitely hasn't been doing that. They're just gone.
So the Tojo Clan...
No. Thanks for your time.
Of course.
(Time for a confrontation... and the <Color:7>vacant lot opposite Public Park 3<Color:Default> is as good a place as any.)
(I think I'll head to <Color:7>Stardust<Color:Default>.)
(Someone's tailing me.)
(Well. It sure has been a long time since I was here. I should get the lay of the land again... <Color:7>New Serena<Color:Default> would be a good place to start.)
I'm sorry. We're not open yet.
Wait⑬ Kiryu-san!?
Nice to see you again.
Can you help us out? We need somewhere private to talk. Mind if we take over the bar for an hour?
Not at all, Kiryu-san. I'm just so happy to see you again.
I'll make sure no one else comes in.
Something to drink?
No, we're fine.
Okay. I'll be in the back, so call me if you need anything.
You've got your privacy. So you better start talking.
Okay. Let me start by laying out Morinaga's big plan.
...Although it might be obvious at this point.
